Container.Name: ModelHub
Container.Overview:
Self-hosted, open 3D print file library manager: STL/3MF/OBJ/STEP/FBX organization, thumbnails, duplicate detection, tagging, semantic search, smart collections, filament inventory and a print queue. AI tagging/search can run against a local Ollama instance (nothing leaves your network) or an external OpenRouter/OpenAI-compatible API using your own key -- switch anytime from the in-app Settings tab. Point "Library Path" at the share where your STL/3MF files already live; nothing is modified on disk, files are only read and hashed.
On first open you'll be asked to create an admin login (or set Admin Username/Password below to skip that screen). Also includes print time/filament weight estimates, projects that track the electronics/parts/supplies each build needs (with an exportable shopping list and a Supplies page for what you already own) and subtract the filament used when a project is marked printed, matching of your models (one by one or your whole library) to their Printables/MakerWorld listings (pictures, designer, license, tags, parts lists), a Search page across sites with a wishlist, a print log, duplicate cleanup, backup and restore, several logins, printer status and G-code upload, a page for every model and project with PDF export, a browser extension for one-click import, and optional webhook notifications (ntfy/Discord/Slack).
Container.Changes:
### 2.28.0 Quiet hours and a daily digest for notifications (alarms always come at once), e-mail (SMTP) as another way to be told, and a printer can be marked out of service so it is never suggested or started without asking. A camera wall page shows every printer's latest camera picture (stills that refresh every few seconds) for a tablet or TV, and each picture can be used as a still camera in Home Assistant. Each printer card has a temperature chart for the last day and a "Why can't it connect?" check; a network scan finds Klipper and OctoPrint printers; Settings has a log viewer and a support bundle with no secrets in it. New tables and columns are added automatically.
### 2.27.0 Sign-in: two-step sign-in with an authenticator app and single-use backup codes, single sign-on (OpenID Connect: Authentik, Keycloak, Authelia and others) and LDAP, all in Settings under Sign-in security; single sign-on and LDAP accounts are never the administrator. Every sign-in and security change is recorded (administrator only) and the activity record can be exported as CSV. Shop orders: WooCommerce and ShipStation are checked every ten minutes, and Shopify or WooCommerce can send signed web hooks; each order is made once. Customers can open a quote link and accept or decline it. The shelf can refill itself by queueing prints when parts fall below their minimum. Etsy, eBay and TikTok Shop are not offered (they need approved developer apps). New tables and columns are added automatically; the image now includes ldap3.
### 2.26.0 Prometheus and Grafana: switch on /metrics (Settings) and import the ready dashboard. More ways to be told: Telegram, Pushover, Gotify, Matrix and Bark with quiet and loud messages, plus structured fields on the webhook, and a Telegram bot (/status, /queue, and, only if you allow it, pause, resume and confirmed cancel) with one status message edited in place. A printer can wait for its plate to be cleared before the next print (a button, an API call, or the camera seeing an empty plate twice), published over MQTT. The "match my whole library" job no longer stops because one site keeps failing: that site is left out for the run, named in the message, and models it could not search are tried again next time. No new settings are required; new columns are added automatically on first start.
### 2.25.0 Slicers can now send sliced files straight to Model Hub: switch on the virtual printer (Settings, Slicer) and add it in PrusaSlicer, OrcaSlicer or Cura as an OctoPrint or Moonraker printer with an API token. The file is kept with the model it is named after and queued if the slicer says upload and print; nothing is ever started, and files it cannot place wait in an inbox. Thingi10K and Objaverse can be added as sources (Settings, Dataset sources: each list is downloaded once on request): Thingi10K is searched by name, designer and tag; Objaverse by category, with names and licences from Sketchfab and models converted to an STL scaled to 80 mm. No new settings are required; new tables are added automatically on first start.
### 2.24.0 From a third round of research: a Report under Stats (jobs, success rate, print time, filament and cost by printer, material and customer, with filters and printer utilisation); maintenance that also falls due by grams, prints or failed prints, predicts its date, can be flagged as a problem and can follow Bambu fault codes; Discord messages with a camera picture, optional started, progress and paused messages and your own wording; a shelf of finished parts with a minimum, that orders can take from and that fills itself from prints; CAD, slicer and scene files kept with a model (stored only); slicer project 3MF files that could not be read are now read directly; and a corpus checker for stress-testing. No new settings are required; new columns and tables are added automatically on first start.
### 2.23.0 From a second round of research: budgets that reserve money when a print is queued, charge it when it finishes and can stop a dispatch once spent; a sliced file kept for one printer; an exact-colour switch for routing; orders that move to printing and ready by themselves; queued prints held while a Home Assistant sensor is alerting (door open, chamber hot); pause, resume or cancel on several printers at once; a queue timeline with when each print would finish if started now; a printer login that can start and stop prints but change nothing else; and a most-used sort for the library. No new settings are required; new columns and tables are added automatically on first start.
### 2.22.0 Maintenance keeps a history of what was done, with an optional note for each. Print settings can be saved as named profiles and put on any model. A status page for a wall display shows each printer's state and progress and the queue without a sign-in; it is off until you switch it on, its link holds a secret, and it never shows addresses, keys or camera links. No new settings are required; new tables are added automatically on first start.
### 2.21.0 From a round of research into what other print-farm and library tools offer: waiting prints get a priority, a hold box and an optional needed tag (printers can carry tags), with ordering by priority or shortest first. Starting a print checks the spool has enough filament. A G-code file with no weight gets one worked out from its length. Spools can be looked up in the Open Filament Database (downloaded once on request). Orders can be imported from a shop's CSV export (Shopify, Etsy, WooCommerce, eBay). No new settings are required; new columns are added automatically on first start.
### 2.20.0 Starts can be kept apart: set a number of minutes between starts and/or a most printers printing at once (Settings, Print planning) and Model Hub says why it is waiting before it starts a print, with a way to start anyway. A watched printer can optionally be paused (never cancelled) after three bad camera looks in a row. Phones with NFC (Chrome on Android) can write a spool's link to an NFC tag and scan it to open the spool. No new settings are required; new columns are added automatically on first start.
### 2.19.0 A printer's smart plug (Tasmota or Shelly) can measure what each print used, shown in kWh in the print history. When a printer reports a failed print, the share of filament that went into it comes off the spool (a switch in Settings turns this off). Models can be starred (each login has its own stars) with a Starred filter in the Library, and collections show a cover picture you can choose. No new settings are required; new columns and tables are added automatically on first start.
### 2.18.0 A printer's camera can be watched for a failed print by your own local vision model (off until you switch it on; it only tells you, it never stops a printer). A model's page has a mesh check and can make a repaired copy (holes filled, faces turned the right way) as a new version. Share a model file to Model Hub from your phone's share menu. A Creators page lists everyone who designed something in your library. Spools loaded in a printer remind you when they are due for drying. Settings shows where your disk space goes. No new settings are required; new columns are added automatically on first start.
### 2.17.0 New Orders tab for prints made for other people (customers, due dates, prices, progress from the queue, profit, spreadsheet export). A cost calculator on each model's page works out the cost and a price to ask (filament, electricity, machine time, failed prints, margin). Waiting prints get a suggested printer (bed size, spool loaded, how busy), assignable in one click and undoable. Spoolman can be imported from and exported to, and finished prints can report their grams to it. No new settings are required; new columns and tables are added automatically on first start.
### 2.16.0 Multicolour prints are counted properly: a sliced file's filaments can be mapped to the printer's slots and each spool loses its own grams. Printers can be paused, resumed and cancelled from Model Hub. Each printer can have a bed size, so models that are too big for it are flagged and the Library can be filtered to what fits. Backups can also be sent to a folder or a WebDAV server. Fixed: importing a file while the background scan was indexing the same file could fail. No new settings are required; new columns are added automatically on first start.
### 2.15.0 Bambu Lab printers (LAN mode) can be added: their state shows like the others, finished and failed prints are logged, and the AMS slots are read, with one-click loading of the matching spools and remaining weights. New: printer maintenance schedules (print hours and days, with a notification when due), an optional weekly summary, "Open in a slicer" buttons (PrusaSlicer, OrcaSlicer, Bambu Studio), suggested settings from how a model's prints went, playing time-lapse videos in the page, and a new source: the Internet Archive's copy of Thingiverse (search and download, no account). No new settings are required; new columns and tables are added automatically on first start.
### 2.14.0 A model that failed before now warns you (on its page, in the Print Queue and on the Calendar) with the usual reason and a tip, and the Library can be filtered to models that failed before. Printers with several spools (AMS, MMU, toolchangers) can have spool slots: say which spool is in which slot, and a queue entry that names a slot is counted against the spool in it. Print entries can keep a link to their time-lapse video, and the administrator can find it on the Klipper or OctoPrint printer. The Calendar can repeat a week of planned prints onto the next weeks, with undo. No new settings are required; new columns and tables are added automatically on first start.
### 2.13.0 Failed prints are now tracked: mark a print as failed and say why (bed adhesion, warping, clog...), a stopped print is logged as a failure by itself, and Stats shows what failures wasted. Failures never count as a print. The Calendar can be viewed per printer, warns when a spool will run out before the plan is done (with an optional notification), and prints made can get a photo straight from a phone camera. New source: Smithsonian 3D, with its print-ready museum models searchable and downloadable. No new settings are required; new columns are added automatically on first start.
### 2.12.0 Print times now learn from your own prints: a model you have printed before is queued with the time it really took, and estimates for new models are corrected by how far off they usually are. Printers can have a camera address; when a print finishes its picture is kept as the print's photo. New Calendar tab to plan which day each waiting print is for (days that need more time than your printers have turn red, prints can be planned automatically and undone, and a .ics file works with phone calendars). A collection, or the whole library, can be shared as a read-only gallery link. No new settings are required; new columns are added automatically on first start.
### 2.11.0 Library information can be exported (JSON or CSV) and imported back or from a spreadsheet made elsewhere. New filing rules file a model by itself (a tag or a collection) from its online listing's category, tags, title or designer, and can be undone. The Print Queue can assign jobs to printers, shows each printer's waiting time and can send the next job to it. Optional Home Assistant / MQTT publishing of printer state and library numbers (Settings; off until a broker is set). STEP models can get pictures from the browser (Library > Make STEP pictures). No new settings are required; new tables are added automatically on first start.
### 2.10.0 Each model's page can keep sliced files (G-code or a sliced 3MF) and reads the estimated time, filament weight and layer height from the slicer's comments; a kept G-code file can be sent to a printer without a slicer in the container. New Recent changes page (Library) records who changed what, and bulk edits can be undone (right after applying one, or from that page). Sliced files are not part of backups. No new settings are required; new tables are added automatically on first start.
### 2.9.0 New Stats tab: prints, filament used and its cost, print time per month, most printed models, filament by material, printer success rate and how much of the library has never been printed. Model Hub now tells the administrator when a newer release is out (checked once a day, can be switched off in Settings, Updates). Settings, API tokens makes read, write or import keys for scripts and other programs. Behind an HTTPS proxy the login cookie is now marked Secure (the README has a short reverse proxy guide). No new settings are required; new tables are added automatically on first start.
### 2.8.0 Several files can now be grouped as versions of one model (v1, v2...), with a "Latest versions only" filter. Models and projects can be shared through a secret read-only link (no login needed; notes and print history are never shown, downloads and costs only if you allow them, links can expire or be revoked). Filament spools and supplies get printable QR labels that open the right item when scanned with a phone. The 3D view has Measure, Section and Compare-with-another-version tools. No new settings are required; new tables and columns are added automatically on first start.
### 2.7.0 The Library has filters (designer, license, collection, project, linked or not, has notes, and "fits my printer's bed" using the build volume you enter in Settings), more sort orders and saved searches. Press Select to change many models at once: add or remove a tag, collection or project, set the designer or license, or queue them. Each model's page has a "What worked" panel for its print settings and a Print again button that queues it with the filament of its last print. Filament spools keep a price history, and spools that are running low appear on the shopping list. Saved backups made in the same second no longer replace each other. No new settings are required; new tables and columns are added automatically on first start.
### 2.6.0 Model Hub now does some things by itself: a saved backup every week (or day, or off; the newest 7 are kept), a look for new uploads from designers you follow, warnings when a filament spool or supply runs low, an optional daily check of linked listings, and noticing when a printer finishes a print (the print is logged for the model and its queue entry completed, taking the filament off the spool). Settings, Notifications has a test button and a switch for each kind of message. The release builds now use current GitHub Actions. No new settings are required; new tables are added automatically on first start.
### 2.5.0 More than one login: the first account stays the administrator, and Settings, People adds members (use everything except Settings, backups and user management) and read-only viewers. Model Hub can be installed on a phone (Add to Home screen) and its pages fit a phone screen. Print Queue has a new Printers panel: add Klipper/Moonraker or OctoPrint printers, see their status, and send them a G-code file (or slice a model first when you give the container a slicer and your printer profile); nothing starts unless you ask. Also fixes the 3D view going blank on every model page after the first one you visit until the page was reloaded. No new settings are required; new tables are added automatically on first start.
### 2.4.0 New Following tab: follow a designer from one of their listings and see their new uploads (Printables and Sketchfab need no account; Thingiverse uses your token). Matches has a Listing updates check that flags linked models whose online listing changed (description, pictures, tags, license, files) so you can refresh them. Projects now show what they cost: give your spools a price (Filament tab) and optionally an electricity price per kWh (Settings), and the project page and PDF add up filament, parts and electricity. The wishlist gained priorities, a got-it-elsewhere status, CSV export, pasting a list of links, and importing your Thingiverse likes or a collection. No new settings are required; new tables and columns are added automatically on first start.
### 2.3.0 New Backup section in Settings: download or save on the server a copy of everything Model Hub knows (tags, collections, projects, supplies, links to listings, notes, wishlist, print log and pictures; passwords and site keys are left out), and restore it later; a restore first saves the current data so it can be undone. Every model's page now has a print history (date, rating, filament used, notes, photo), finishing a print-queue job logs it, and the Library can show only printed or never-printed models. New duplicates page (Library, Review duplicates): identical files are grouped, one is kept with the tags, collections, projects, notes and print history of the others, and the extra files can optionally be deleted (each is checked first). No new settings are required; new tables are added automatically on first start.
### 2.2.0 New Wishlist tab: save listings from the Search tab or a listing page (with a note), see which are already in your library, and add the whole list in one go. A listing's page now lists every file it has, so you can tick just the ones you want before adding it (Printables' single STLs as well as its model pack). Two more sites that need no account can be searched and downloaded: Wikimedia Commons (3D files) and NASA 3D Resources (Apollo landing sites, satellites and more). Search now asks all sites at once, so one slow site no longer holds up the rest. The browser extension manifest is updated for Firefox 128 or newer (tested in Firefox 157). No new settings are required; a new table is added automatically on first start.
### 2.1.0 New Search tab: search your library and every connected site at once, open any result for a full preview page, and add models to your library with one click, or tick several and add them together (Printables and Thingiverse files are downloaded by the server, kept to model file types only, and linked to their listing with pictures and details). MyMiniFactory and Cults3D can now be searched too: add their API keys in Settings, where each site has a Test button. Settings also lets you download the browser extension, which now works on Thingiverse, MyMiniFactory, Cults3D and Sketchfab pages as well (and in Firefox), and downloads with your own login for sites that need it. Matches has a Linked models list that can unlink many models at once. No new settings are required; new tables and columns are added automatically on first start.
### 2.0.0 Every model and every project now has its own page instead of a popup (the back button works, and each page has an address you can bookmark). The model page shows the 3D view, details, editable tags, notes, its online listing, and the projects and collections it belongs to. The project page has an editable name, description and notes, its models with pictures and filament, the parts list, and an Export PDF button that makes a one-file summary of the whole project. The library now only lists and imports model files (.stl .3mf .obj .step .stp .fbx): zips, notes and other files in the library folder are ignored, importing a zip keeps just the models inside, and Settings has a cleanup for older entries. Model matching now also searches Sketchfab, and Thingiverse once you paste a free access token in Settings. The matching job can optionally link clear winners automatically (listed for a second look), and a project can use the filament a MakerWorld listing recommends, matched to your own spools. No new settings are required; new tables and columns are added automatically on first start.
### 1.9.0 New Matches tab: a background job searches Printables and MakerWorld for every model in your library that is not linked yet and builds a review queue of the closest listings. Link one, tick and link many at once, or mark a model as skipped; nothing is linked without your say-so. In a project you can now import the parts list from a MakerWorld listing (Bambu Lab store items with links and prices, plus the designer's own list), edit the rows, and add them in one go. Match thumbnails use small versions of the pictures, and the database now waits longer for a lock instead of failing while a background job is running. No settings changes; new tables are added automatically.
### 1.8.0 Shopping list export: download the Projects shopping list as CSV or text, or copy it, and optionally combine identical parts from different projects. New Supplies tab for the electronics, parts and supplies you already own, with low-stock flags, locations and CSV export; the shopping list shows how many you have in stock. Models can now be matched to their Printables or MakerWorld listing: search by name or paste a link, then pull in the title, designer, license, description, tags and pictures (pictures are shrunk and saved under /config/source_images). Models imported with the browser extension from those sites are matched automatically. The library API now returns each model's tags, so tags show up in the viewer. No settings changes; new tables and columns are added automatically on first start.
### 1.7.1 Fixes the browser holding on to the previous version's page after an upgrade (new tabs and features not showing up until a manual hard refresh). The page and its scripts are now versioned, and the server tells browsers to check for changes before reusing cached files, so updates appear on the next page load. No settings changes.
### 1.7.0 New Projects tab. A project groups library models and keeps a parts list (electronics, parts, supplies) with how many are needed vs. owned, unit cost and a buy link. Filter to the projects that still need parts, or open the Shopping List for everything missing across unfinished projects with an estimated total. Add a model to a project from its viewer, then give it one or more filament spools with grams each (the Estimate button fills grams from the print estimate). When a project is set to printed (or done) that filament is subtracted from inventory exactly once; moving it back to planning or building restores it. No new settings; new tables are created automatically on first start.
### 1.6.0 Fixes the app still crashing when a scan runs. Loading a model file takes many times its size in memory (a 35MB Bambu Studio project needed 4GB, a 262MB STL 3GB), and that happened inside the app itself -- one large file anywhere in the library could get the whole container killed on every scan. Model files are now parsed in a separate, memory-limited worker process: if a file is too big it's indexed from a preview instead (the .3mf's embedded thumbnail, or a streamed render of the STL), and if the worker dies anyway only that file is affected. New optional setting: Mesh Worker Memory (MB), blank for automatic. Thumbnail regeneration gets the same protection, and the 3D viewer now asks before loading huge models.
### 1.5.0 Fixes an OOM crash loop and a 3D viewer error on multi-part .3mf project files (Bambu Studio / OrcaSlicer, which split each plate/object into its own file inside the .3mf). Scanning one of these could consume 15GB+ of RAM computing mesh watertightness and OOM-kill the container on every launch -- since the background scan runs on startup, this could look like the app crashing right after launching, and any files past that one in scan order (including in subfolders -- scanning was already recursive, it just never got that far) would never get indexed. Also extracts the slicer's own embedded preview from .3mf files when present instead of rendering our own, and fixes the live 3D viewer failing to open these same multi-part files.
### 1.4.0 Fixes the actual root cause of Tag All crashing the container: an oversized AI response (e.g. a local vision model stuck generating past a sane length) could get fully buffered into memory in a single network call fast enough to OOM the container in seconds -- too fast for the 1.3.0 fix's periodic checkpointing to help. AI responses are now streamed with a hard size cap so that can't happen, generation length is capped as a second line of defense, and the tagging job now checks the container's actual memory usage before every model and stops itself cleanly (instead of the kernel silently killing the container) if it's running critically high.
### 1.3.0 Tag All no longer risks crashing/hanging on large untagged libraries: the batch job now periodically releases database state instead of holding everything in memory for the whole run, per-model failures are logged instead of silently swallowed, and a crash mid-job no longer leaves the tagging state stuck. Also adds a configurable 3D preview/thumbnail color (Settings -> 3D Preview) plus a Regenerate Thumbnails maintenance job (contributed by @justindgreen), which runs in parallel and can resume if interrupted.
### 1.2.0 Large-library fixes contributed by @justindgreen: the initial/background scan now runs off the main event loop so the WebUI and health check come up immediately instead of appearing stuck on big libraries; mesh/thumbnail memory use is now bounded so indexing a large library no longer grows memory unboundedly; concurrent scans are rejected cleanly instead of racing on SQLite; the Library view is now paginated with full-library search instead of only showing the first 200 models.
### 1.1.0 Live STEP/STP viewer (client-side WASM via occt-import-js, no server round trip), rate limiting on the login endpoint (5 attempts / 15 min per IP), and a mobile-responsive UI (scrollable tab bar, stacked forms, full-screen viewer modal, larger touch targets).
### 1.0.0 Initial release. STL/3MF/OBJ/FBX live viewer, AI auto-tagging + semantic search (local Ollama or API), smart collections, filament inventory, print queue with volumetric/slicer-based estimates, session auth, webhook notifications, a Printables/MakerWorld browser extension, and PUID/PGID support so files under /config are owned by a real host user instead of root.
Container.Requires: Optional: an Ollama container (install the official "ollama" template from Community Applications first) if you want local AI instead of an API key.

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: Port for the Model Hub web interface

Config.Name: Library Path
Config.Description: Folder containing your STL/3MF/OBJ/STEP/FBX files. Read-only usage: files are hashed and thumbnailed, never modified.

Config.Name: App Config/DB
Config.Description: Where the SQLite database, thumbnails, and settings are stored.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: Unraid's nobody user -- keeps /config editable from the host

Config.Name: Scan Interval
Config.Description: Seconds between automatic background library scans.

Config.Name: Mesh Worker Memory (MB)
Config.Description: Memory ceiling for the separate process that parses model files during scans. Leave blank for automatic (half of the container limit or host RAM, 1-8 GB). Files needing more are still indexed, from a preview (a .3mf's embedded thumbnail, or a streamed render of an STL) instead of a full parse. Raise it only if you have RAM to spare and want full stats on very large files.

Config.Name: Ollama Host
Config.Description: Address of your Ollama container/instance for local AI tagging. Only used when AI mode is set to 'local' in the app's Settings tab.

Config.Name: Ollama Vision Model
Config.Description: Vision-capable Ollama model used for auto-tagging thumbnails.

Config.Name: Ollama Embed Model
Config.Description: Ollama embedding model used for semantic search.

Config.Name: Admin Username
Config.Description: Creates the admin login automatically on first start. Leave blank to set it up from the WebUI's first-run screen instead.

Config.Name: Admin Password
Config.Description: Paired with Admin Username above. Leave both blank to use the in-app setup screen instead (recommended -- avoids the password sitting in plain text in the container's env).

Config.Name: Slicer CLI Path (advanced)
Config.Description: Optional: absolute path *inside the container* to a headless slicer CLI binary (e.g. an extracted PrusaSlicer/OrcaSlicer AppImage) for exact print time/filament estimates instead of the built-in volumetric approximation. Bind-mount the binary in via 'Add another Path' first, then point this at it.
